title: The editing session walk adds captions the way a person does
goal: The one walk that plays a whole edit at Next defaults says the captions 'wrote themselves, nothing was pressed'. Since 2026-09-28 the app writes captions only when asked, so that line tells anyone reading the walk the wrong thing, and the walk never proves the Add Captions command a person actually uses still works inside a full edit.
notes: Scripts/playtest/an-editing-session-walk.json step 3 uses action captionsWriteQuietly (PlaytestHarness.swift ~3944, which calls editor.writeCaptions(quietly:) directly); seed text line 3 and note line ~52 say 'Nothing was pressed: the captions wrote themselves'. The user's ask: captions-only-when-you-ask-for-them (done 2026-09-28). objectives.json now words the focus success the same way (this pass). Find a walk step that presses a menu row or a playtest control by name (lock-safety: a by-name lookup makes the walk refuse on a locked screen; prefer the app's register of panel controls or a menu row read without opening it, see PlaytestLockSafety.swift). Walk-only change: no Sources edit expected unless the Add Captions control needs a playtest name.
acceptance: an-editing-session-walk asks for captions through the app's own Add Captions command (the timeline's + menu, the clip's right-click Audio row, or the menu bar, whichever a first-time user meets first) instead of the harness's quiet step, and waits for them
Its seed and step notes say captions were asked for, and no longer say they wrote themselves
The walk still runs green at Next defaults with its 7 real pictures, within the rotating check's time, and still fails on a blank frame
Anything left rough is written into this task's log, or filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar

log.note: Before building: the + menu (Add Track, Captions) is the timeline's own ask and is lock-safe as a panelMenu read without opening; the right click is not lock-safe and the inspector button only shows once Edit mode and the Captions section are up, so the + menu is what the walk now uses. A non-quiet ask picks the Captions layer and switches to Edit; the walk's later steps (select tool, Cmd K, Delete) are unaffected because the cuts act on the clip in hand. Baseline run of the old walk gave the same 2-cut picture as the new step, so the swap changes nothing downstream.

Found while comparing pictures: the walk cut at 0:08 then 0:04, and a cut leaves the piece BEFORE it picked, so Delete threw away the first 4 seconds, not the middle the note claimed, and the dissolve went on a seamless join. Swapped the cut order (0:04 then 0:08); now the middle goes, the captions for 0:00-0:04 stay, and the dissolve blends Copying 135 into Ready 0 across a real jump cut. Same 12.94s length, everything after unchanged.

left rough: the walk proves the + menu row works, not a pointer click on the + button (panelMenu chooses inside the app). captions-on-demand-walk covers the right click and the inspector button; no task filed, as no person-visible defect was seen. 20 other walks still use captionsWriteQuietly as setup for features that are not about captions, which is what the quiet step is for.

an-editing-session-walk now asks for captions through the timeline's + menu (Add Track, Captions) and waits for them to land; seed and step note say they were asked for. Also fixed the cut order so Delete takes the middle piece the walk describes and the dissolve sits on a real jump cut. Ran green at Next defaults with no flags, 7 real pictures, 57s, blank-frame check unchanged; Scripts/test.sh green (11502 tests). Commit cf7c6df4.
